# atlas-vfx: plate to Nuke, all in ComfyUI
**Shot:** DSCF3000 S2-S3 (Fuji X-H2, F-Log2), Nuke frames 1130-1297.

**1 Plate** reads the camera file, F-Log2 F-Gamut into ACEScg through our ACES 2.0 OCIO config.

**2 Camera** imports the tracked camera as an **Alembic (.abc)** (here Nuke's export, any app works), in metres, sitting on the plate's frames.

**3 Track check** projects a grid card on the deck through that camera. If the grid sticks, the camera is right.

**4 Grass** Z-Image draws two clumps of grass, BiRefNet cuts them out, and each becomes a card standing in the real world (metres from the camera, on the lawn). Card Project renders each through the camera for every frame.

**5 Element** a generated performance clip (load your own in the Load Video node): BiRefNet cuts it out, it stands on the deck at its real height, lifted 1.5 stops so it reads in the dusk. A **depth holdout** (MoGe plate depth, metres) hides it wherever the plate is nearer the camera, so the stair railing passes in front. *end_mode* hold / pingpong / loop decides what happens after the clip ends.

**6 Deliver** writes the camera (.chan, USD) and a Python script that builds the whole comp in Nuke: plate Read, every layer, the camera.

All layers are premultiplied ACEScg EXRs with Nuke frame numbers, under `atlas-vfx-work\DSCF3000`.

**7 Watch the shot** comps the plate with the element and both grass cards (back to front, through the ACES 2.0 view) and plays it as a movie.

*Run time on ws: about 15 minutes from cold (mostly writing 4K EXRs), seconds when nothing changed.*

# Sensor pass (rolling shutter + lens as STMaps)
LTX renders come out global-shutter and rectilinear. The plate is not: the X-H2 reads its sensor top to bottom over ~30.9 ms (4K HQ), so every row is a slightly different camera. Convention: take the plate's camera OFF the plate, generate in clean space, put it back ON the render last.

**Plate side (tracked here in ComfyUI):** Camera Import (group 2) + Plate Depth's folder feed **Sensor RS Maps**. **Sensor Readout Solve** measures the readout from the solve's tracks and wires in; readout_source picks measured or the typed 30.9 ms. The .abc camera is a global-shutter solve: its poses already soak up most of the skew, and the deck reprojection test showed the physical 30.9 ms on top makes alignment worse. So this graph uses the measured residual (~7 ms). Switch to typed 30.9 ms only with a camera from a rolling-shutter-aware solve. **Sensor Lens Maps** takes the lens from the camera (none on this solve) with typed overrides, plus CA and vignette.

**Into LTX:** Sensor Apply, *remove camera*, takes the plate to clean space (LTX Prep cannot take an IMAGE plate yet: see UPSTREAM_TODO).

**Out of LTX:** Sensor Apply, *apply camera*: vignette (linear) -> CA + distortion -> RS. With ltx_prep connected it reads the render's frame range and crop windows from LTX Prep.

Every map is a Raw float ZIP EXR with Nuke Reads (sensor_rs.nk, sensor_lens.nk) next to it.
